reason: Rays are the primary branches of an umbel (the PO synonym 'first order inflorescence branch' fits). The word 'rays' also means ray florets of Asteraceae and wood rays, so it needs an inflorescence context.
Umbel rays are the primary inflorescence branches.
A gametangium is an archegonium or antheridium of bryophytes and ferns. In flowering plant floras 'sex organs' means stamens and pistil, or the androecium and gynoecium.
Same as 'sex organ': it means stamens and pistil in seed plants, not gametangia.
'Organes sexuels' means stamens and pistil in French floras, not gametangia.
As a bearer, 'pubescence' is the hair covering, which is the indumentum.
A reddish-brown hair covering is an indumentum. The colour is a separate quality.
The order 'secondary' is lost. Statements would mix with the plain bracts of the primary axis. Bracteole is only a synonym when the bract is on a secondary axis.
The order 'secondary' is lost, as for the singular.
The order 'secondaires' is lost, as for the English rule.
A colpus is a pollen aperture. PO 'canal' is a groove or channel of an organ, which is a different thing. Pollen apertures need a pollen aperture class, not canal.
Colpus is a pollen aperture, not a canal or groove of an organ.
'Colpé' means 'having colpi', which is a quality word and not a part. It is also a pollen aperture, not a canal.
Perigone (perianth) segments are tepals.
Perigone segments are tepals.
'Segments du périgone' are tepals.
The seed scale of a conifer cone is the ovuliferous scale, which is a PO synonym of megasporophyll.
A fruiting scale is a cone scale of a conifer, or a scale in fruit in Carex or Atriplex. It is not the grass fertile lemma. For a conifer cone, PO_0009027 would fit, but the word is ambiguous.
The galea is only the hooded upper lip, and in orchids a hood made of sepals and petals. The class 'corolla lip' loses 'upper' and 'hooded', and does not fit the orchid sense.
The sex 'pistillate' is lost. The spike inflorescence class would take statements about all spikes, and not only those with female flowers.
Calicle (calyculus) is a PO synonym of epicalyx.
Disk scales are scale-like parts or segments of the disc, not the whole floral disc. The meaning also varies by family, so it should not be mapped to the whole disc.
'Lip' is either the orchid labellum or the corolla lip (see the rejected 'lip limb'). Without the family the labellum lobe may be wrong. It is correct only for orchids.
The epichile is the distal part of the orchid labellum, so its lobes are labellum lobes.
'Stipe' is the stalk of a fern frond, a pappus, a pollinarium or a gynophore. The PO class 'stalk' loses whose stalk it is. It needs the organ.
'Stipes' is a stalk of an unnamed organ, so the stalk class loses the organ.
The stipe of a pollinarium is the stalk of that one organ. The generic stalk class loses 'pollinarium'. It needs a container rule.
A stem scale may be a scale leaf (cataphyll) or an epidermal scale (trichome, as in ferns). Mapping it to a trichome is correct only for some plants.
Rhizome scales are usually scale leaves, or epidermal scales in ferns. The two senses cannot be told apart, so the trichome class is doubtful.
Same as 'stem scale': scale leaves versus epidermal scales.
Secondary veins are secondary leaf veins. The 'per side' count is handled by the counted-part pattern.
Lateral nerves are secondary veins in Malesian floras.
Perianth members may be sepals and petals in a differentiated perianth. Tepal is right only for an undifferentiated perianth.
Pleiochasium is a PO synonym of cyme inflorescence.
Plural of pleiochasium.
A twig is a PO synonym of branch. 'Leafy' only describes the twig.
Plural of leafy twig, same as the singular.
A branchlet is a PO synonym of branch.
A sheath scar is the scar left by a leaf sheath. A culm sheath is a modified leaf.
A culm sheath scar is the scar of a culm sheath (a modified leaf).
'Lip' may be the corolla lip or the orchid labellum, and the median position is lost. It is correct only for orchids.
'Lip' may be the corolla lip or the orchid labellum, and the median position is lost.
The labellum is named, so the median lobe of the labellum is a labellum lobe. This follows the earlier note on rejected generic lobes.
Connecting veins are cross-veins between the secondaries, a PO synonym of tertiary leaf vein.
The position 'inner' is lost. Inner and outer phyllaries often differ, and statements would mix.
The position 'inner' is lost. Inner and outer phyllaries often differ.
Coronal filaments (for example in Passiflora) are thread-like parts of the corona. They are not corona lobes, which are the lobes of an asclepiad or daffodil corona.
Coronal filaments are not corona lobes.
Same part as spathe limb, written with a hyphen.
The labellum is named, so its lateral lobe is a labellum lobe. This follows the earlier note on rejected generic lobes.
